entries.subject: SDSS DR9 color HiPS
entries.finding: A 2250 x 2250 px hips2fits cutout of CDS/P/SDSS9/color, 15 arcmin wide at the HiPS's 0.40 arcsec per pixel. 70 of the 74 Gaia DR3 stars brighter than G = 19 in it have a star within 4 px of their requested places. Shallow: the outer arms are faint.

entries.subject: Observatory press images of NGC 4536
entries.finding: ESA/Hubble potw1715a covers 2.45 x 2.72 arcmin of a galaxy whose RC3 isophotal diameter is 7.6 arcmin: the centre only. The ESO and NOIRLab image archives return nothing for NGC 4536.
entries.revisitWhen: A whole-disc photograph is published under an attribution licence.

entries.subject: DESI Legacy Surveys DR10 color HiPS
entries.finding: Deeper than SDSS, but its cutout of this field carries a satellite trail and colored patches of sky beside the disc.
entries.revisitWhen: A later release cleans the field.

entries.subject: Disc tilt and position angle
entries.finding: Leroy et al. (2021) give inclination 66.0 +/- 2.9 deg and position angle 305.6 +/- 2.3 deg. Lang et al. (2020) fit 67.7 deg and 305.5 deg to the CO velocity field, so the angle is the receding side's.

entries.subject: Catalogues of NGC 4536's nebulae and clusters
entries.finding: The PHANGS-MUSE nebular catalogue (Groves et al. 2023, J/MNRAS/520/4902/catalog) has no rows for NGC 4536. No other catalogue of its nebulae or clusters was searched for in this change, so the bank has no dots.
entries.revisitWhen: CDS is searched for its HII regions, clusters or remnants with sky positions.

entries.subject: Bulge
entries.finding: Salo et al. (2015), S4G Pipeline 4, table 7, NGC4536, model _bd: a Sérsic bulge (35.0% of the light, magnitude 10.99, half-light radius 5.84″ = 0.43 kpc, n = 1.466, axis ratio 0.451, PA 124.86°) and an exponential disc (65.0% of the light, scale length 50.68″ = 3.73 kpc, axis ratio 0.435, PA 125.48°, face-on central surface brightness 20.837, 19.933 as projected on the sky). Used as published; the half-light surface brightness the bake needs, 16.834 mag per square arcsecond, follows from the bulge's magnitude, radius, index and axis ratio. At the disc's 66.0° the bulge's axis ratio is one an oblate spheroid in the disc plane can show (intrinsic 0.21).
